text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000531 bills 99215 at roughly three times the complexity-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, but the few returned charts support the billed level, so the evidence is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not explained by a sicker panel: in the by-complexity table this provider's 99215 share runs about two to three times the all-provider share in every band, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions, and the low-complexity sample shows 99215s on single routine diagnoses such as uncomplicated E11.9, I10 or J06.9 (e.g., C0251638, C0251435, C0251371). Against that, none of the 5 documented 99215 claims were documented below the billed level, but this is too few charts to judge (records cover only about 2% of claims), so the documentation neither confirms nor clears the pattern. There is a possible soft signal in the supported examples: C0251432, a one-condition hypothyroidism visit, is documented at high MDM, and three of the four supported 99215 notes have no time recorded, so a reviewer should check whether these notes are templated or cloned rather than specific to the visit. The first step should be a targeted records request for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed (especially the 0-condition and repeat-patient ones such as C0251876/C0251878), reviewing whether MDM is specific to the visit. Until more charts return, the pattern is consistent with possible upcoding but not established."}
